account upon the fulﬁllment of the relevant terms and conditions by the concerned Establishment speciﬁed in the applicable scheme
guidelines and in case of non-fulﬁlment of such terms and conditions, the Establishment is liable to pay the monthly stipend amount in full
to the apprentice.
(3) During the second year of apprenticeship training, there shall be an increase of ten per cent. in the prescribed minimum stipend
amount and further 15 per cent. increase in the prescribed minimum stipend amount during the third year of apprenticeship training.
(3) The apprentice shall abide by the rules and regulations of the establishment in all matters of conduct and discipline and safety and
carry out all lawful orders of the employer and superiors in the establishment.
(4) The provisions of Chapters III, IV and V of the Factories Act, 1948 (63 of 1948), shall apply in relation to the health, safety and welfare
of the apprentices as if they were workers within the meaning of that Act and when any apprentices are undergoing training in a mine, the
provisions of Chapter V of the Mines Act, 1953 (35 of 1952) shall apply in relation to the health and safety of the apprentices as if they
were employed in the mine.
(5) The daily and weekly hours of work of an apprentice while undergoing practical training in a workplace shall be determined by the
employer subject to the compliance with the training duration, if prescribed and apprentice shall be entitled to such leave and holidays as
are observed in the establishment in which he is undergoing training.
(6)If personal injury is caused to an apprentice, by accident arising out of and in the course of his training as an apprentice, his employer
shall be liable to pay compensation which shall be determined and paid, so far as may be, in accordance with the provisions of the
Employee‘s Compensation Act, 1923 (8 of 1923).
(7)The apprentice shall be governed by the rules and regulations (applicable to employees of the corresponding category) in the
establishment in which the apprentice is undergoing training.
(8)Every apprentice undergoing apprenticeship training in an establishment shall be a trainee and not a worker and as such the provisions
of any law with respect to labour shall not apply to or in relation to such apprentice.
(9)The employer shall make suitable arrangements in his establishment for imparting a course of apprenticeship training to the apprentice
in accordance with the provisions of the Act and the rules made thereunder with the approval of the Central or State Apprenticeship
Advisor.
(11)It shall not be obligatory on the part of the employer to oﬀer any employment to the apprentice on completion of period of his
apprenticeship training in his establishment.
(12)The stipend for a particular month shall be paid on or before the tenth day of the following month.
(13)No deduction shall be made from the stipend for the period during which an apprentice remains on casual leave or medical leave and
the stipend payment module on the apprenticeship portal shall require the establishment to update the unauthorised leaves and stipend
amount payable to each candidate for the month.
(14)Where the contract of apprenticeship is terminated through failure on the part of any employer in carrying out the terms and
conditions thereof, such employer shall be liable to pay the apprentice compensation under these rules.
(15)The progress in apprenticeship training of every apprentice shall be assessed by the employer from time to time and every apprentice
who completes his apprenticeship training to the satisfaction of the employer shall be granted a certiﬁcate of proﬁciency by that employer
which shall be the basis for further assessment or certiﬁcation by the concerned awarding body.
(16)The conditions for the degree apprenticeship shall be the following, namely:
(i) the employer shall provide the apprenticeship training as per the approved program in accordance with the contract and within
the overall provisions of the Act;
(ii) the academic Institution shall deliver the course as per the approved course curriculum including the management of the
apprenticeship component undertaken in partnership with the industry partner or employer;
(iii) mapping and reporting apprenticeship contracts and other related compliance on the portal shall lie with the academic
institution or any authorized agency working on its behalf;
(iv) the employer shall permit apprentices to attend scheduled academic sessions in between the training period either at the on-
the-job training premises or at the academic institution campus as the case may be.
(17)In case of any applicable Government scheme for apprenticeship promotion, the establishment or apprentice or guardian (in case of
minor apprentice) warrant and conﬁrm that they have studied, understood, and agree to comply with the scheme guidelines pertaining to
them, and these Guidelines shall be made available in the public domain and may be updated from time to time.

Delivery Manager - Al Projects
Fill these in before posting: location . salary range . benefits . work mode . application email. Everything else is ready to copy and paste.
Location: [Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu / Hybrid] Experience: 4-8 years Employment type: Full-time, permanent Salary: [₹XX-XX LPA + performance-linked variable]
About Adople Al
Adople Al builds production Al systems for enterprise clients in healthcare and financial services - agentic document extraction, Al data analysts, voice agents and enterprise Al workflows. We work on real deployments in regulated environments, not proofs of concept.
The role
We are looking for a Delivery Manager who is accountable for work getting finished - not for producing plans and status reports.
You will own delivery across our client engagements: breaking work down, assigning it clearly, tracking it honestly, and giving clients dates we can actually meet. If you enjoy removing friction more than adding process, you will do well here.
What you'll do
Own end-to-end delivery of Al projects for enterprise clients, from kickoff to handover
Break work into clearly assignable tasks - one owner, one date, and acceptance criteria anyone can verify Run the delivery board day to day: track work in progress, cycle time, blockers and aging items Produce estimates you can defend, with ranges and confidence levels rather than single-number guesses Manage client-side dependencies (sample data, SME availability, security reviews, sign-offs) as first-class items in the plan, with named owners and dates
Escalate on a fixed schedule rather than on instinct, so nothing sits stuck for days unnoticed
Run reviews, retrospectives and post-mortems that produce a small number of changes that actually happen Own and configure our delivery tooling (Jira, Linear or similar), keeping it simple rather than adding to it Communicate with clients early, specifically and honestly - especially when a date is at risk Continuously remove steps, meetings and approvals that no longer earn their place
What success looks like
First 30 days: every active item has an owner, a deadline and written acceptance criteria; baseline delivery metrics published
By 90 days: measurably faster delivery cycles, 80%+ of commitments met on time, and no client surprised by a missed date
By 6 months: estimates calibrated against actuals, and a delivery process that is smaller than the one you inherited
What you need
4-8 years in project or delivery management for software, data or Al projects, including at least 2 years personally accountable for client-facing deadlines
Strong grasp of estimation and scheduling: decomposition, effort versus calendar time, dependency and risk management
Technical literacy - able to read an API spec, a data pipeline design or a model evaluation report and ask the right follow-up questions. You do not need to write code, but you cannot be bluffed Hands-on experience with Jira, Linear, Asana or similar, including configuration and reporting Excellent written English. Most of this role is writing clearly enough that no follow-up conversation is needed Comfortable pushing back on scope - with a reason and an alternative, not just a refusal Willing to overlap with US time zones for part of the working week
Good to have
Domain exposure to healthcare (HIPAA, HL7/FHIR, revenue cycle management) or financial services (KYC/AML, regulatory reporting)
Experience delivering LLM or ML-based systems, including evaluation design and QA of non-deterministic output
Agency or services background running several concurrent client engagements Familiarity with Agile, Kanban, WIP limits, or Lean delivery practices
PMP, CSM or PMI-ACP certification (useful, not a substitute for delivery track record)
What we offer
Real ownership of delivery across our client portfolio, with the authority to make decisions Production Al work in regulated, high-value domains rather than pilots that go nowhere A small team with short decision paths and no layers to route through
[Salary range] plus performance-linked variable pay [Health insurance / other benefits] [Hybrid / remote / on-site] working arrangement
How to apply
Apply through this portal with your CV.
In your application, please include a short note (a few lines is enough) about one project you ran that slipped - what caused it, and what you changed afterwards. We are far more interested in the diagnosis than in the outcome.

Notes for posting
Title. "Delivery Manager - Al Projects" is the recommended posting title because candidates search for "Delivery Manager" and "Project Manager". Do not post it as "Task Completion Manager" - it reads junior and
returns almost no search traffic. Good alternatives, depending on how you want it to land:
Technical Project Manager - Al Delivery Project Manager - Al & Data Projects Senior Delivery Manager - Al Solutions
Per-portal adjustments.
Naukri: keep the description under roughly 5,000 characters. If you need to trim, cut "What success looks like" and shorten "Good to have" - the key-skills field does most of the matching work here, so make sure it is complete.
LinkedIn: post as written. The "What success looks like" section performs well with senior candidates and is worth keeping.
Indeed: move "How to apply" to the very top; Indeed applicants often skim only the first screen.
One thing to decide before you post. This role only works if the person has real authority. Confirm internally that they can reject an incoming request, enforce a work-in-progress limit against an engineer's objection, and change tool configuration without seeking approval. If not, you are hiring a coordinator - reword the responsibilities accordingly, or strong candidates will find the gap in interview and withdraw.

Effect of Drying and Cooking Pretreatments on Drynaria quercifolia Extracts and Their Anti-Inflammatory Activity
Summary: Drynaria quercifolia (oak-leaf fern) is traditionally used to manage inflammation due to its rich phytochemical profile, but its therapeutic potential can vary based on how the plant material is processed and stored. This project evaluated the anti-inflammatory activity of D. quercifolia extracts prepared under different pretreatment conditions, including freeze-drying and cook-drying. Anti-inflammatory efficacy was assessed using in-vitro assays such as protein denaturation inhibition, enzyme/protein inhibition, and membrane stabilization methods. The findings indicated significant differences in bioactivity across processing protocols, with freeze-dried samples showing better retention of bioactive compounds and the highest inhibitory activity. In contrast, cook-drying reduced activity, likely due to heat-induced degradation of active constituents. The study highlights the importance of optimizing and standardizing pretreatment conditions to improve the reliability, quality control, and pharmaceutical potential of D. quercifolia extracts.
